name: latch_channel_state_to_hardware
description: Stores a clamped difference of two channel fields into a record, and when a pending flag is set it clears that flag and writes several channel words to the custom chip registers. The register list also names the DMA and interrupt control registers.

name: run_step_sequence_with_countdown
description: Calls a three-step routine in sequence, then, when a global flag is set and a countdown byte reaches zero after decrementing, calls the routine once more. It returns the value produced by the last call.

name: countdown_then_invoke_handler
description: Checks a record flag and, when a handler pointer is set, decrements a countdown byte in the record and calls the handler once it reaches zero. Otherwise it returns the value it started with.

name: advance_three_phase_level
description: Steps a 16-bit level through three phases using increments and limits read from a seven-byte table, and it moves to the next phase when the level crosses the phase limit. Its phase counter is reset when the table's threshold byte is reached.

name: run_four_channel_sequencer
description: Loops over four channel records of 74 words each, reading command bytes from a sequence pointer, where the escape byte sets a stored value and any other byte ends the read. It runs the per-channel timers and calls update routines for each record, and its register list names DMACON and INTENA.

name: enter_command_interpreter_stub
description: A three-instruction entry that jumps into the command interpreter body, which reads sequence bytes and programs channel state. It only forwards control and holds no logic of its own.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Two-instruction fragment in a gap that the decompiler decoded as code. It falls into the command interpreter body and is not a meaningful standalone routine.

name: start_command_stream_from_pointer
description: Loads a sequence pointer from the channel record and runs the same command interpreter body, with the pointer stored back into the record first. It is a three-instruction entry, so its behaviour is the interpreter's.

name: scale_byte_then_run_interpreter
description: Stores a sequence byte multiplied by a parameter word into a channel field, then enters the command interpreter body. It is a five-instruction entry with no logic beyond that store.

name: store_divided_period_then_interpret
description: Divides a fixed constant by a sequence byte and stores the quotient in a channel word, then enters the command interpreter body. It is a five-instruction entry.

name: sum_byte_run_into_field
description: Sums a counted run of sequence bytes, scales the total by a parameter word and stores it in a channel field, then enters the command interpreter body. The decompiler decoded it from a gap, so it may not be a true entry point.

name: copy_fifteen_word_table_entry
description: Clears the low two flag bits in a channel record, copies a fifteen-word entry selected by a sequence byte from a fixed table into the record, and zeroes several accumulators. It then enters the command interpreter body.

name: enter_interpreter_from_gap
description: A two-instruction fragment in a gap that the decompiler decoded as code. It falls into the command interpreter body and does not stand alone.

name: load_fourteen_byte_table_entry
description: Selects a fourteen-byte entry from a fixed table by a sequence byte, copies three words and two longs of it into the channel record, and enters the command interpreter body.

name: start_stream_from_pointer_table
description: Loads a sequence pointer from a table indexed by a sequence byte and enters the command interpreter at that pointer. It is reached through a gap that the decompiler decoded as code.

name: copy_three_word_pairs_strided
description: Copies two word fields from one record to another and steps the record pointer forward by one word, repeating this three times. The pairs are copied at fixed offsets, so the loop fills consecutive channel entries.

name: copy_two_word_pairs_strided
description: Copies two word fields between offsets of a record and steps the pointer by one word, repeating this twice. It performs the same kind of copy as its neighbour, with one fewer pass.

name: stub_undecompiled_routine
description: The decompiler timed out on this twelve-instruction routine, so no pseudo-code is available. Its only recovered facts are that it is address-taken and has a single caller, so its behaviour is not established.

name: patch_jump_stubs_in_memory
description: Stores its argument in a global and calls through a pointer taken from it. It then writes call, jump, no-operation and return instruction words into several fixed memory locations and calls through a stored pointer, and its text reference names the program Akira.

name: return_fixed_constant_value
description: Returns a fixed constant of 524288 and does nothing else. It is a two-instruction routine whose only role is to supply that value to its caller.

name: replace_branch_with_nops
description: Checks a word at a fixed offset from its pointer, and when it holds a branch opcode it overwrites the four bytes there with two no-operation instruction words.

name: mark_empty_string_flag
description: Calls through a function pointer held in a global record, then if the first byte of the string it is given is zero, it sets the byte at a second pointer to 255. It returns the value it received in the data register.

name: wait_on_task_message_port
description: Program entry that finds the current task and then waits on its message port, reading messages from it. It calls four other routines, and the decompiler timed out, so only the library calls and instruction count are established.

name: call_constant_return_helper
description: A routine of nineteen instructions that refers to a programmer credit string and calls a two-instruction routine, which loads a constant into the data register. The decompiler timed out, so its logic beyond those facts is not recovered.

name: run_title_command_sequence
description: Loops over a list of command records, calling a dispatch function for each step and branching on its result to advance, reset, or jump to another record. It stops when a record holds the end marker, and it refers to the title executable.

name: restart_command_sequence_state_three
description: Sets a state value to three and resets the record pointer to the start of the command table before re-entering the same dispatch loop. Its code path is otherwise the same as the title sequence loop.

name: run_sequence_from_state_two
description: Sets a state value to two, resets the record pointer to the start of the command table, and runs the dispatch loop. It otherwise shares the title sequence loop's branches.

name: retry_sequence_from_state_two
description: Re-enters the command sequence loop from its state-two reset when the dispatch result is minus one. It is a branch target of the sequence loop rather than a separate entry.

name: advance_command_sequence_record
description: Reads the next command byte from the current record, sets the record's state, and continues the dispatch loop. It is the entry used when a record has been stepped forward.

name: run_command_sequence_with_resets
description: Runs the command sequence dispatch loop with several reset branches, calling a dispatch function for each step and advancing through records. It is the largest of the title sequence variants, with fifty-eight instructions and six callers.

name: dispatch_sequence_result_loop
description: Loops over command records, calling a dispatch function and branching on its result: zero advances to the next record, minus one and minus two reset to the table start, and any other negative value jumps to an error exit that stores a fixed code.

name: store_error_code_and_call
description: Writes a fixed error code into a stack-relative slot, calls one routine, and returns. It is a three-instruction error exit.

name: allocate_cleared_memory_or_halt
description: Asks the Exec memory allocator for a cleared block and returns the address when it is valid. If the allocation fails and a size field is large enough it returns a fixed marker value, and otherwise it sets two words and spins in an endless loop.

name: match_case_insensitive_filename
description: Walks a list of zero-terminated names and compares each with a string by folding letters to uppercase. On a match it stores the first character minus the digit one as a number and calls routines, and it refers to the title executable name.

name: store_digit_offset_then_scan
description: Stores the first input character minus the digit one into a global, scans the string to its terminating zero byte, clears a flag and calls four routines, one of them conditionally. It is the tail of the filename match routine.

name: clear_hunk_blocks_after_end
description: Scans an AmigaDOS hunk-format list until it reaches the end-of-hunk code, counting blocks, then zero-fills each memory region in a pointer-and-length table until a null pointer. It sets up its state before the scan.

name: zero_hunk_tables_until_end
description: Advances through a hunk-format list counting words until the end-of-hunk code, then zero-fills the memory regions in a pointer-and-length table. It is the variant that skips the initial state setup and calls an empty stub.

name: dispatch_hunk_record_by_type
description: Handles one AmigaDOS hunk record by its type: a header record sets block sizes and counts, code and data records copy words into the block table, bss records reserve zeroed blocks, and relocation records add base addresses. It returns a status value to its caller.

name: return_four_times_first_word
description: Returns four times the first word of a counted list, or zero when that count is zero. It is a small size calculation used by the hunk loader.

name: skip_length_prefixed_records
description: Steps through a list of length-prefixed records, advancing by each record's count plus two, until it reaches a zero count. It returns nothing.

name: follow_indexed_link_chain
description: Follows a chain of links in which each node holds an index at offset four, moving to a new address computed from that index, until the index is zero. It returns nothing.

name: load_hunk_block_table
description: Skips a zero-terminated list, reads a three-field header, and writes a table entry for each block with its high address flags masked out. It then waits on a status check and calls a routine that reports the result.

name: load_hunk_block_table_direct
description: Reads a three-field header directly from its input and writes a table entry per block with the high address flags masked out. It differs from its neighbour in that it does not skip a leading list, and it reports through a routine.

name: report_size_overflow
description: Compares a stored value with a fixed threshold and, when it exceeds it, waits for a status bit to clear. It then writes the value and its excess over the threshold to the output and calls a reporting routine.

name: stub_empty_return
description: A one-instruction routine that returns immediately and does nothing.

name: wait_then_write_status_words
description: Busy-waits while a flag bit is set, then writes three values to a fixed output location and calls a routine. The facts list the fire-button and disk status register and the background colour register as touched.

name: copy_counted_longs_to_slot
description: Copies a counted run of longwords into a destination selected from a table by an index. It does nothing when the count is zero.

name: append_length_record_to_list
description: Finds the first empty entry in a pointer list and writes a pointer, a count and a zero terminator there, with the pointer taken from a table by index. It does nothing when the count is zero.

name: write_table_entry_triple
description: Writes a table pointer chosen by index, a count, and a zero terminator to a given address. It is the fixed-slot form of the list append routine.

name: apply_offset_relocations
description: Walks zero-terminated records of offsets and adds a base value from a table to the longword at each offset. It stops at the terminating zero count.

name: empty_return_routine
description: A routine with a single return instruction that does nothing. It is the same empty return as its neighbours.

name: move_byte_block_backward
description: Saves the first four bytes at a destination, moves a counted byte block backward from its end to that destination, and restores the saved bytes after calling three routines. It shifts a byte block in place.

name: decode_bitstream_into_buffer
description: Builds lookup tables from a block of byte counts, then decodes a bitstream by shifting bits out of a word and copying bytes or byte pairs from the tables into the output until the output count runs out. It is a bit-level decompressor, with the table build running before the decoding loop.

name: decode_symbol_stream_bits
description: Reads bits one at a time to find a symbol in a table of counts and offsets, then writes one byte or two bytes to the output until the counter is exhausted. It is the inner decoding loop of the bitstream routine before it.

name: decode_bits_with_offset_table
description: Writes a pair of bytes from a table offset by a stored value, then decodes the next symbol from the bitstream and repeats until the byte count is used up. It shares the bit reading and table lookups of the decoder family.

name: build_lookup_tables_then_dispatch
description: Clears a 256-entry word table, fills it from a set of constants and an arithmetic sequence keyed by a stored code, and then makes an indirect call through a computed entry. The indirect target cannot be recovered, so only the table work is established.

name: clear_bytes_endless_loop
description: Writes zero bytes to successive addresses in an endless loop with no exit, so it never returns. Its only effect is the byte clearing.

name: reset_hardware_state_block
description: Writes a clear-all mask to the enable registers, copies eight longwords from a state record into hardware-facing globals and back, then calls routines. The register list includes the timer, copper pointer, DMA and interrupt registers.

name: configure_interrupt_enable_block
description: Sets the enable bit on a value read from a hardware register, writes clear-all masks, copies a state block, and then writes a fixed word to a custom chip register. It is a configuration routine for interrupt and DMA state.

name: install_handler_pointers_in_record
description: Writes one routine pointer into eight consecutive slots of a record, starting sixty bytes in, after clearing a set of enable bits. It also copies a state block and calls a routine.

name: set_exception_handler_slots
description: Stores a routine pointer into eight consecutive slots of an exception record, the same handler setup as its neighbour. It is a nineteen-instruction setup that also calls a return-from-exception routine.

name: copy_state_and_set_masks
description: Writes clear-all masks to a control value, copies a block of eight longwords, and writes saved values back to the hardware-facing globals. It calls one routine and is one of the state save and restore routines.

name: control_cache_when_flagged
description: Reads a four-bit flag from a field of the system base and, when it is set, calls the Exec cache control routine. It also calls a supervisor-mode routine when a size field exceeds a threshold.

name: spin_forever_stub
description: A three-instruction routine with no exit that loops forever. It writes nothing and returns nothing.

name: set_request_word_seven
description: Stores the value seven into a hardware-facing global and returns. The register list names the interrupt request register.

name: set_request_word_112
description: Stores a fixed constant of 112 into a hardware-facing global and returns. The register list names the interrupt request register.

name: set_request_word_1920
description: Stores a fixed constant of 1920 into a hardware-facing global and returns. The register list names the interrupt request register.

name: set_request_word_6144
description: Stores a fixed constant of 6144 into a hardware-facing global and returns. The register list names the interrupt request register.

name: set_request_word_8192
description: Stores a fixed constant of 8192 into a hardware-facing global and returns. The register list names the interrupt request register.

name: wait_for_vertical_beam_transition
description: Polls the vertical beam position register until its position bits reach a fixed value, then waits until they leave it. It returns after one full transition.

name: wait_for_vertical_beam_line
description: Waits until the vertical beam position bits reach a fixed line, then waits for them to move off it. It is the line-based counterpart of the transition wait.

name: read_keyboard_serial_code
description: When a flag bit is set, it clears a block of sixty bytes, decodes the byte read from the keyboard serial register by inverting and rotating its bits, and stores the mapped key code. It then acknowledges the interrupt request.

name: build_copper_color_pointer_list
description: Clears a 24-longword area, splits twelve-bit colour words into red, green and blue fields, and writes copper move instructions for the colour registers and the high and low halves of the bitplane pointers. It finishes by writing the last copper entries.

name: copy_copper_list_for_mode
description: Copies ninety-six longwords, each spaced ten bytes apart, from a table chosen by the low two bits of a control byte into a copper list. It then stores the list address and calls a routine, and the facts name the copper pointer and jump registers as touched.

name: accumulate_and_pack_nibbles
description: Clears a 24-word area, then over seven steps calls a routine and adds three stored deltas to each of seven three-word groups. It packs the high nibbles of the three sums into one word per step.

name: scan_disk_track_entries
description: Selects a drive through bits in the CIA port register, then compares five-character names against a table, and on a match copies a block of bytes into a buffer. It also calls the copper-list and interrupt routines and uses a fixed marker string as its sentinel.

name: enter_disk_track_scan
description: A three-instruction entry into the disk track scanning loop, which compares names and copies blocks. It only forwards control to that loop.

name: resume_disk_track_scan_loop
description: Resumes the disk track scanning loop by decrementing a retry count and then selecting the next track before matching names. It shares the name comparison and copy code of its neighbours.

name: scan_track_entries_with_retry
description: Runs the disk track scanning loop with a setup stage that prepares the output pointer, then compares names and copies matched blocks. It is one of several entry points into the same loop.

name: scan_track_entries_from_match
description: Starts the name comparison at the marker string and then runs the disk track loop, copying matched blocks. It is one of several entry points into the same loop.

name: call_mask_update_helper
description: Calls a routine that merges fixed bit patterns into a control byte and then returns. It is a two-instruction wrapper.

name: return_without_action
description: A routine the decompiler reduced to a plain return, so it has no effect that the evidence shows.

name: decode_disk_sector_with_checksum
description: Checks the sector number derived from the track position against eleven sectors per track, then decodes a 128-longword sector block from raw data. It XOR-accumulates the words and returns once the masked checksum is zero, using an alternating-bit mask.

name: decode_disk_sector_from_header
description: Sets a control byte, compares the sector number from the track position with the header value, and decodes a 128-longword sector block with the same checksum test as its neighbour. It omits the earlier range check.

name: search_sync_word_then_decode
description: Searches the raw track for the disk sync word, compares the header's track and sector bytes with the expected values, and then decodes the sector block with checksum verification. It loops over several sync candidates.

name: decode_sector_after_sync_match
description: Decodes a sector block with checksum verification after a sync match, and retries the header search when the check fails. It is a variant of the sector search routine with a different checksum mask.

name: stub_no_operation_return
description: A routine that does nothing and returns immediately.

name: step_disk_head_to_track
description: Compares the current track position with a new one and steps the disk head by the difference, one step per call. It sets the direction bit from the sign of the difference and stops early when the drive status reports an error.

name: set_disk_track_and_step
description: Stores a new track number and steps the disk head by the difference from the old track, stopping early if the drive status reports an error. It is the variant of the head step routine that does not wait first.

name: step_head_with_retry_count
description: Repeats a head step call up to a count, stopping when a status bit clears, and sets a failure byte when the drive stops responding.

name: issue_disk_controller_command_a
description: Pulses a control bit, writes three command values to fixed disk controller addresses, and waits for the busy bit to clear. The last command value is twenty-five.

name: issue_disk_controller_command_b
description: Pulses the same control bit, writes zero and then fourteen to the controller addresses, and waits for the busy bit to clear.

name: issue_disk_controller_command_c
description: Pulses the control bit, writes zero and fourteen to two controller addresses, then a command of twenty-five, and waits for busy to clear.

name: write_disk_controller_command_pair
description: Writes zero, a byte passed in the data register, and a command of twenty-five to fixed controller addresses, then waits for the busy bit to clear.

name: repeat_until_counter_zero
description: Calls a routine repeatedly while a counter register is nonzero, then returns. It is a plain repeat loop.

name: sample_status_bits_until_one
description: Shifts thirty-two sampled status bits into a longword and records in a record byte whether all sampled bits were set. It repeats until the returned value equals one.

name: update_drive_select_bits
description: Clears one control bit chosen by a register value, sets a group of fixed control bits, and clears a bit chosen from a second register offset by three. It is a control register update.

name: set_motor_control_bits
description: Sets a group of fixed control bits and clears one bit chosen from a register value offset by three.

name: enable_drive_select_bit
description: Sets one control bit chosen by a register value, sets a group of fixed control bits, clears a second bit chosen by an offset, and sets the group again.

name: initialise_runtime_state_from_record
description: Copies a 100-byte block and a 40-byte block from a supplied record into fixed memory, stores its fields into globals, and calls a routine through a stored pointer. It then configures the copper and interrupt registers and clears interrupt request bits.

name: wait_until_status_bit_set
description: Calls a routine repeatedly until bit seven of a status value is set, then returns. It is a status wait loop reached through a gap in the code.

name: wait_for_flag_then_clear
description: Waits until a global flag becomes nonzero, clears it, and returns the data register unchanged. It is called by many routines as a simple handshake.

name: wait_until_counter_reaches_value
description: Waits while a global counter is below a value passed in the data register, then clears the counter and returns.

name: wait_for_beam_position_transition
description: Polls the vertical beam position register until its position bits reach a fixed value, then waits until they leave it. It is the same transition wait used elsewhere in the program.

name: write_five_bitplane_pointers
description: Writes five bitplane pointer pairs into a copper list at a fixed address, advancing each pointer by forty bytes from a base address. Each pointer is stored as a high and a low word beside its copper register number.

name: write_five_bitplane_pointers_alt
description: Writes the same five bitplane pointer pairs as its neighbour into a second copper list at a different fixed address.

name: alternate_double_buffer_pointer
description: Switches a global pointer between two fixed buffer addresses on each call, using an XOR with one to choose the next buffer.

name: read_joystick_direction_bits
description: Reads the joystick movement register and the fire button bits, combines them into direction and fire flags in a global, and clears bits that are no longer set. It calls a library routine first when a device value is set.

name: run_text_input_state_machine
description: Handles one input event by moving a cursor state up, down, left, or right, and writes a computed code into a fixed text buffer when a key code arrives. It programs a block of hardware words through a register pointer and calls twenty-one routines.

name: clear_control_code_byte
description: Reads a byte through a pointer and, if it equals one of several control codes, clears it to zero. It has no other effect.

name: advance_byte_stream_pointer
description: Walks a stream of bytes through a global pointer, zeroing each byte it consumes and moving to the next. When the stream ends it resets the pointer to a fixed sentinel and stores a value into a record slot.

name: accumulate_deltas_into_packed_words
description: Clears a 96-word area, then over thirty-two steps adds three stored deltas into each group of three words. It packs the high nibbles of the sums into one word per group and advances a step counter by eight while it stays below a limit.

name: subtract_deltas_into_packed_words
description: Subtracts stored three-word deltas from a fixed buffer over thirty-two steps and packs the high nibbles of each result into one word. It decrements a step counter by eight on each step and does not clear the buffer first.

name: subtract_deltas_sixty_four_steps
description: Subtracts stored three-word deltas from a fixed buffer over sixty-four steps and packs the high nibbles of each group into one word. It does not clear the buffer first.

name: subtract_deltas_sixty_four_alt
description: Repeats the sixty-four step delta subtraction of its neighbour on the same fixed buffer, with the same packing of high nibbles.

name: subtract_deltas_and_set_levels
description: Subtracts deltas into the fixed buffer over thirty-two steps, and after each step sets four record fields to a level that drops by two per step. The packing matches its neighbours.

name: increment_frame_counter
description: Advances a counter global by one, calls a routine when the counter was zero, and resets a second global to a fixed register value. The facts show the interrupt request register is touched.

name: reset_pointer_slot_table
description: Stores a fixed base address into four pointer slots and zero into four others, then clears several globals and sets a record field to fifteen.

name: set_pointer_slots_for_index
description: Points four slots at a table entry selected by an index, each entry sixteen bytes apart from a base, and copies one byte from a second table into each slot's neighbour. It then sets the low four bits of a global.

name: update_audio_channel_pointers
description: Walks four audio channel records and, for each active one, writes its sample pointer and length to the matching audio channel registers. It then enables the channels through the DMA control word and clears the state fields.

name: halt_in_endless_loop
description: Loops forever with no exit and no effect. The decompiler marks the block as unreachable from the rest of the code.

name: dispatch_pending_interrupt_bits
description: Checks four interrupt request bits in turn and calls a handler for each one that is set, then stores the masked request value. The facts show the interrupt request register and its read-back are touched.

name: toggle_interrupt_flag_128
description: Flips a toggle global and, when it returns to the off state, stores the bit value 128 into a second global and clears it. The facts show the interrupt enable register is touched.

name: toggle_interrupt_flag_256
description: Flips a toggle global and, when it returns to the off state, stores the bit value 256 into a second global and clears it. The facts show the interrupt enable register is touched.

name: toggle_interrupt_flag_512
description: Flips a toggle global and, when it returns to the off state, stores the bit value 512 into a second global and clears it. The facts show the interrupt enable register is touched.

name: toggle_interrupt_flag_1024
description: Flips a toggle global and, when it returns to the off state, stores the bit value 1024 into a second global and clears it. The facts show the interrupt enable register is touched.

name: fade_audio_channel_volumes
description: Fades all four audio channel volume registers from a maximum down in steps of two over thirty-two passes. Before the fade it sets up interrupt handlers and reads bytes until an escape code, calling twenty routines in total.

name: accumulate_deltas_to_two_buffers
description: Clears a 96-word area, then over thirty-two steps adds three stored deltas per group and packs the high nibbles of each sum into two destination buffers at once.

name: subtract_deltas_to_two_buffers
description: Subtracts stored three-word deltas over thirty-two steps and packs the high nibbles of each result into two destination buffers at once. It does not clear the buffer first.

name: parse_anim_chunk_header
description: Checks that a memory block starts with the four-character tag ANIM and that its first chunk is tagged BODY, then records the chunk's data address and size. It initialises two colour and pointer tables and returns zero on success, or minus one when the tag does not match.

name: initialise_animation_colour_tables
description: Clears a global, fills a ramp of colour-register words in a copper table, and converts four palette entries into split colour nibbles. It waits for the blitter to be idle before starting its copies and calls five routines.

name: copy_longword_block_650
description: Copies six hundred and fifty longwords from one address to another, one per loop pass. It has no other effect.

name: step_palette_fade_phases
description: Steps a counter-driven palette fade: while the counter is nonzero it adds deltas to four colour entries and packs them into the copper table, and at the end of the count it sets a terminal value. A second branch subtracts the deltas in the reverse direction and resets the counter to 150.

name: initialise_palette_from_source
description: Converts thirty-one source palette words into split colour nibbles in a working table, clears three counters, and fills a block of ninety-three words with a fixed colour value. It then sets two globals.

name: copy_longword_block_9000
description: Copies nine thousand longwords from one address to another, one per loop pass. It has no other effect.

name: shift_words_right_six
description: Shifts each of ninety-six words from one buffer right by six bits into a second buffer.

name: shift_words_right_five
description: Shifts each of ninety-six words from one buffer right by five bits into a second buffer.

name: advance_anim_frame_state
description: Advances an animation state through a set of counters, branching on the current state value. It splits a frame word into three colour nibble fields, writes five bitplane pointer pairs through the same routine as the other bitplane writers, and calls six routines.

name: copy_rectangle_into_frame_buffer
description: Copies a rectangle of longwords from a source buffer into a frame buffer, advancing the destination by a row stride after each row. The width and height come from register arguments.

name: copy_rectangle_with_source_stride
description: Copies a rectangle of longwords into a frame buffer, advancing both the source and the destination by a row stride after each row. It calls seven routines.

name: copy_longword_block_6050
description: Copies six thousand and fifty longwords from one address to another, one per loop pass. It has no other effect.

name: copy_ninety_six_words
description: Copies ninety-six words from the source pointer into a fixed working buffer.

name: decode_run_length_bitplanes
description: Decodes a run-length compressed image into four bitplanes: a negative count repeats the following byte and a positive count copies literal bytes. Output rows are forty bytes apart and each plane follows the previous at a fixed stride, with one hundred and eighty rows.

name: start_anim_delta_chunk
description: Checks that the block begins with the four-character tag DLTA, skips its header, programs a copper pointer and a blitter transfer, and decrements a frame counter. It returns zero while frames remain and minus one otherwise.

name: call_for_nonzero_slots
description: Checks five consecutive words from a table and calls a routine for each nonzero one, in order.

name: apply_anim_xor_delta_ops
description: Applies an IFF ANIM style XOR delta to a bitplane. For each of forty columns it reads opcodes that XOR a run of literal bytes into the destination, repeat a byte, or skip rows by a count, with rows forty bytes apart.

name: run_anim_playback_setup
description: Sets up the copper and interrupt state, waits in an input loop that ends on an escape code, and then runs a thirty-two pass loop that subtracts deltas from the working buffer and packs colour nibbles into two tables. It calls fifteen routines.

name: accumulate_deltas_clearing_work_area
description: Clears a ninety-six-word work area and a twelve-word area, then over thirty-two steps adds deltas and packs the high nibbles into two destination tables. It calls two routines.

name: accumulate_deltas_alternating_tables
description: Over thirty-two steps, adds deltas into two destination tables on even steps and always adds a short four-group delta into a second pair of tables. It packs the high nibbles of each sum and calls one routine.

name: parse_anim_body_setup_copper
description: Checks the ANIM tag and BODY chunk as its neighbour does, then fills two copper tables with bitplane pointers at a larger stride and clears their colour words. It converts four palette entries into split colour nibbles and returns zero on success or minus one on a tag mismatch, calling six routines along the way.

name: decode_run_length_bitplanes_narrow
description: Decodes a run-length image into four bitplanes of twenty-four bytes per row over one hundred and eight rows. A negative count repeats the following byte and a positive count copies literal bytes, with each plane placed at a fixed stride.

name: start_anim_delta_frame
description: Checks for the DLTA tag, skips its header, and programs a copper pointer and a blitter transfer with a different control word. It then decrements a frame counter and returns zero while frames remain, or minus one otherwise.

name: call_nonzero_entries_in_table
description: Calls a routine for each nonzero word in a five-entry table, in order. It has the same behaviour as its neighbour.

name: apply_anim_xor_ops_narrow
description: Applies an IFF ANIM style XOR delta to a bitplane with twenty-four columns and a twenty-four byte row stride. Opcodes XOR literal bytes into the destination, repeat a byte, or skip rows.

name: continue_anim_xor_delta_ops
description: Enters the middle of the same XOR delta decoder and writes the remaining bytes of the current row with a pending repeat count. It is a resume point rather than a separate routine.

name: setup_anim_playback_copper
description: Writes bitplane pointers and colour words into two copper tables, copies a table of words into the working buffers, and splits four palette entries into colour nibbles. It programs the blitter with a fixed transfer, calls three routines, and toggles a selection global.

name: copy_strided_frame_blocks
description: Copies a frame of one hundred and eight blocks, each four rows of five longwords, from a packed source into a destination whose rows are spaced by a fixed stride. The source advances six longwords per block.

name: queue_blitter_frame_copy
description: Programs a blitter copy whose source offset advances by a 120-byte step for the current frame index, choosing one of two buffers by a flag. It counts frames down and handles a special index value of fifteen by checking a marker byte.

name: start_two_blitter_copies
description: Waits for the blitter to be idle, then programs two blitter copies from fixed source addresses into fixed destinations with the same size setting.

name: render_text_glyph_rows
description: Reads a string and, for each character, either clears a column of forty-nine entries for a space or looks up the character in a glyph table and copies its forty-nine-row bitmap into two buffers. Each row in the buffers is twenty-four bytes apart.

name: render_text_glyph_columns
description: Reads a string and copies glyph columns from a lookup table into a buffer, with each glyph stored as twenty rows forty bytes apart. A character with the high bit set moves to the next line, advancing the output by 960 bytes.

name: fix_up_table_offsets
description: Walks a table of records terminated by a negative value and rewrites each record's offset as a running sum of the previous step and a stored width. It runs only when a counter global is zero.

name: reset_anim_frame_state
description: Resets an animation player's state globals and pointer slots, and when a state value is above one it selects a sequence of blitter setup writes before clearing the state. It calls thirteen routines in total.

name: find_table_index_for_value
description: Searches a ten-entry table for the first entry that is at least the current global value and stores its index in that global. When the index is not nine it also copies a block of bytes for that index.

name: save_text_slot_and_callback
description: Copies a ten-byte text buffer into a slot selected by a global index and records that index in a table. It also copies a one-hundred-byte block into a record and calls a callback stored in the record when one is set.

name: match_text_buffer_against_table
description: Compares a ten-byte text buffer with a table of entries and, on a match, stores the entry number in a global and returns zero. When nothing matches it checks two fixed marker strings, returning minus two when one matches and minus one otherwise, and it sets a bit in a record field for a marker.

name: run_text_entry_input_loop
description: Clears a five-character buffer, programs two blitter copies sized by a state value, and then loops reading input characters. Digits are stored and advance the cursor, backspace and newline edit the buffer, and cursor keys move the position, with the buffer compared against marker strings at the end.

name: handle_text_entry_key_event
description: Handles a single key code within the text entry loop: digits are stored and advance the cursor, newline and backspace edit the buffer, and navigation bits move the cursor. When the buffer matches a marker it sets a flag, and otherwise it returns to the input loop.

name: resume_text_entry_at_digit
description: Enters the text entry loop at its digit path, storing a digit and advancing the cursor before reading further input. It is a resume point into the same loop as its neighbours.

name: resume_text_entry_cursor_move
description: Resumes the text entry loop at its cursor movement step, adjusting the cursor from navigation bits before reading further characters. It shares the editing and marker code of its neighbours.

name: reset_text_entry_cursor_loop
description: Sets the cursor to its end position and enters the text entry loop, which reads characters, edits the buffer, and compares it against marker strings.

name: step_text_cursor_right_loop
description: Advances the text cursor one position, wrapping back to the start after its last place, and then continues the text entry loop. It is an entry into the same loop as its neighbours.

name: reset_text_cursor_start_loop
description: Sets the text cursor to its first position and runs the text entry loop. The loop reads characters, moves the cursor on navigation bits, and compares the buffer against marker strings.

name: resume_text_entry_character_read
description: Resumes the text entry loop at its character read, handling digits, newline and backspace before returning to the input wait. It is a resume point into the same loop as its neighbours.

name: run_text_entry_backspace_loop
description: Runs the text entry loop from its backspace step, clearing a cursor cell and moving the cursor back before reading characters. Digits, newline and cursor movement are handled as in the main loop, which shares the same marker comparison code.

name: resume_text_entry_marker_check
description: Resumes the text entry loop at its marker check, comparing the current buffer with a stored marker string. On a match it sets a flag and returns, and otherwise it repeats the input step.

name: count_down_text_entry_round
description: Decrements a round counter and, while it is not yet negative, clears the five text cells, programs a sized blitter copy, and runs the text entry loop. When the counter goes negative it returns a fixed failure value.

name: set_text_entry_done_flag
description: Sets a per-entry flag byte to all ones and returns. It is the success marker used by the text entry routines.

name: lookup_scrambled_word
description: Looks up a word in a fixed table, indexed by the low twelve bits of a global, and combines it with the global by addition and exclusive-or. It stores the result back into the global.

name: queue_blitter_copy_at_offset
description: Waits for the blitter to be idle, then programs a copy whose source address is derived from a global value, with a fixed destination pair and size word.

name: queue_blitter_copy_from_table
description: Looks up a table entry by a global index, derives a blitter source address from it, waits for the blitter to be idle, and programs the copy.

name: queue_blitter_table_copy_b
description: Like its neighbour, derives a blitter source address from a table entry, but uses a source address two bytes further on.

name: program_blitter_copy_from_arguments
description: Waits for the blitter to be idle, then programs a copy using three address arguments passed in registers and a fixed size word.

name: repeat_until_routine_returns_zero
description: Calls a routine repeatedly until it returns zero, then returns.

name: repeat_until_zero_result
description: Calls a routine repeatedly until it returns zero, then returns. It is the same loop as its neighbour.

name: program_blitter_arguments_copy_b
description: Waits for the blitter to be idle, then programs a copy from three address arguments with different fixed constants from its neighbour.

name: scan_text_cells_until_zero
description: Walks the five-cell text buffer, calling one routine for each cell and a second routine for blank marker cells, until the routine returns zero.

name: scan_text_cells_skipping_blanks
description: Walks the text buffer with a call-and-skip loop, calling a routine for each cell and stepping over blank marker cells, and returns once that routine returns zero.

name: program_blitter_fixed_pair_a
description: Waits for the blitter to be idle, then programs a copy from three register arguments with the same fixed size and modulo constants as its neighbours.

name: program_blitter_fixed_pair_b
description: Waits for the blitter to be idle, then programs a copy from three register arguments using a second fixed pair of size and modulo constants.

name: call_with_temporary_buffer_pointer
description: Calls two routines, saves a buffer pointer global, points it at a fixed buffer while calling a routine, and then restores the saved value.

name: program_blitter_frame_offset
description: Calls four routines, then waits for the blitter to be idle and programs a copy whose source address is a global value plus a fixed offset, with a fixed size word.

name: program_blitter_two_args
description: Waits for the blitter to be idle, then programs a copy using two address arguments and fixed control words.

name: poll_until_routine_returns_zero
description: Calls a routine repeatedly until it returns zero, then returns. It is the same loop as its earlier neighbours.

name: program_blitter_fixed_pair_c
description: Waits for the blitter to be idle, then programs a copy from three register arguments with the same fixed constants as its neighbours.

name: queue_blitter_scaled_offset
description: Waits for the blitter to be idle, then programs a copy whose source address is the global value scaled by three plus a fixed offset, with fixed destination and size words.

name: queue_blitter_table_scaled
description: Looks up a word from a table by a global index, scales it by a fixed factor, adds the global and a fixed offset to form a source address, and programs a blitter copy after waiting for the blitter to be idle.

name: queue_blitter_table_scaled_b
description: Like its neighbour, derives a blitter source from a scaled table word, but programs the copy with slightly different fixed register values.

name: program_blitter_fixed_pair_d
description: Waits for the blitter to be idle, then programs a copy from three register arguments with the same fixed constants as its neighbours.

name: render_text_cell_rows
description: Blits a header area, then maps each cell of a ten-by-ten text buffer to a display code, substituting fixed characters for three control codes. It writes the mapped rows into a line buffer and then fills a table of glyph references for each row.
